## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dung beetle characterized by its shiny metallic green, blue, copper, or reddish coloration, with males often bearing a curved horn on the head. In Florida, it is found in pastures, prairies, pine flatwoods, open woodlands, sandy areas, and other habitats where mammal dung is available. Adults feed on dung and bury portions of it underground for their larvae, helping recycle nutrients, improve soil structure, and reduce waste on the surface.
